text: Quảng Trị plans seven growth poles, corridors linking seaports, airports and border gates

QUẢNG TRỊ - The central province of Quảng Trị has identified seven growth poles and devised plans to develop economic corridors connecting seaports, airports and border gates to create new development space, with the goal of achieving average annual gross regional domestic product (GRDP) growth of at least 10 per cent through 2030.

These are key orientations in a provincial plan to implement the Government's Resolution No 358/NQ-CP on the action programme for implementing the Politburo's Resolution No 27-NQ/TW dated August 28, 2026 on regional development and organisation of national development spaces in the new period.

The seven growth poles include Hòn La-Ba Đồn-Quảng Trạch; Đồng Hới-Hoàn Lão; Đông Hà, Gio Linh, Cửa Việt, Nam Cửa Việt, Triều Bình and Cam Lộ; the Southeast Quảng Trị Economic Zone, Hải Lăng, Diễn Sanh, Mỹ Thủy and Vĩnh Dinh; the Cha Lo International Border Gate Economic Zone; Lao Bảo International Border Gate; and La Lay International Border Gate.
The province plans to develop these growth poles in close connection with its urban network, economic zones and inter-regional transport infrastructure.
It will study and implement a proposal for a free trade zone linked to seaports, airports, economic zones and industrial parks.
Another priority is developing a cross-border economic and trade zone connecting Lao Bảo in Việt Nam with Densavan in Laos.
Transport infrastructure is considered a key factor in connecting development areas.
The province will focus on linking expressways, seaports, border gates and logistics networks.
It aims to put Mỹ Thủy Port into operation and increase the capacity of Hon La International General Port.
Quảng Trị also plans to develop logistics services along the Quảng Trị-Huế-Đà Nẵng corridor, connecting the province with Laos, Thailand and Myanmar.
In the energy sector, priority will be given to major projects, including the Quảng Trạch Power Centre, the Hải Lăng LNG-fired power plant and renewable energy projects.
The province will also coordinate with central authorities to bring natural gas from the Kén Bầu and Báo Vàng fields ashore in Quảng Trị, while promoting electricity imports from Laos.
Regarding urban development, the province will focus on Đồng Hới and Đông Hà and a chain of coastal urban areas linked to economic zones, industrial parks and transport hubs.
Border urban areas will also be developed to facilitate trade and strengthen connections with localities in Laos.
The provincial plan sets 22 specific targets for 2030.
Besides average annual GRDP growth of at least 10 per cent, it aims to raise GRDP per capita to US$5,290 and the digital economy's contribution to 30 per cent of GRDP.
Industry and construction are expected to account for 40.7 per cent of the economic structure, while services will make up 43 per cent.
Total factor productivity (TFP) is set to contribute more than 55 per cent to economic growth.
In social development, the province targets an average life expectancy of 74.5 years, with 68 years of healthy life.
It aims to have 13 doctors per 10,000 people and achieve universal health insurance coverage.
The urbanisation rate is expected to reach 37 per cent, while 60 per cent of communes will meet new-style rural development standards. - VNA/VNS
